community_tested.scenario: amd64/PVE: native OCI LXC daemon driving an iDRAC at 10.0.1.2 over IPMI-over-LAN with line interpolation (FAN_SPEED 01%, HIGH 40%, interp from 57 C, threshold 70 C). Uptime over 5 days, headless, stateless.

tagline.en_US: Hold Dell PowerEdge fans at a fixed duty cycle from CPU temperature over IPMI, with linear interpolation.

description.en_US: Dell iDRAC fan controller drives the fans of a Dell PowerEdge server from its CPU junction temperature over IPMI. It holds a low duty cycle while the server is cool and hands control back to Dell's BIOS profile above a configurable threshold, with optional linear interpolation between two speeds. This profile uses the fork that adds line interpolation. It works on iDRAC 6, 7 and 8, and on iDRAC 9 up to firmware 3.30.30.30; iDRAC 10 and blades are not supported by Dell's IPMI commands.

environment.name: IDRAC_HOST
environment.prompt: IP address of the iDRAC to control, or 'local' for the iDRAC of the host itself

environment.name: IDRAC_USERNAME
environment.prompt: iDRAC username; only required when IDRAC_HOST is not 'local'

environment.name: ENABLE_LINE_INTERPOLATION
environment.prompt: Enable linear interpolation of fan speed between FAN_SPEED and HIGH_FAN_SPEED

environment.name: FAN_SPEED
environment.prompt: Fan duty cycle while the profile is applied, in % (0-100) or hex (0x00-0x64). Default 10

environment.name: HIGH_FAN_SPEED
environment.prompt: Highest fan speed interpolation will reach, higher than FAN_SPEED

environment.name: CPU_TEMPERATURE_FOR_START_LINE_INTERPOLATION
environment.prompt: CPU temperature in degrees Celsius at which interpolation starts

environment.name: CPU_TEMPERATURE_THRESHOLD
environment.prompt: Junction temperature beyond which Dell's BIOS fan mode takes over

environment.name: CHECK_INTERVAL
environment.prompt: Seconds between checks. Default 3 for line interpolation, 60 for non-interpolation

environment.name: DISABLE_THIRD_PARTY_PCIE_CARD_DELL_DEFAULT_COOLING_RESPONSE
environment.prompt: Disable Dell's default cooling response for third-party PCIe cards

container_contract.original_compose:
No official Compose file. Reference docker run command:

docker run -d --name idrac-fan \
  -e IDRAC_HOST=<iDRAC IP or local> \
  -e IDRAC_USERNAME=<iDRAC username> \
  -e IDRAC_PASSWORD=<iDRAC password> \
  -e ENABLE_LINE_INTERPOLATION=true \
  -e FAN_SPEED=01 \
  -e HIGH_FAN_SPEED=40 \
  -e CPU_TEMPERATURE_FOR_START_LINE_INTERPOLATION=57 \
  -e CPU_TEMPERATURE_THRESHOLD=70 \
  -e CHECK_INTERVAL=10 \
  -e DISABLE_THIRD_PARTY_PCIE_CARD_DELL_DEFAULT_COOLING_RESPONSE=false \
  7adrian/dell_idrac_fan_controller_with_line_interpolation:latest

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The project is a fork of tigerblue77's Dell iDRAC fan controller that adds linear interpolation of fan speed. It ships a Docker image driven by environment variables; there is no official Compose file, only a documented docker run command and an .env.example.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: The source model is reconstructed from the documented parameters and translated into one native OCI service.
adaptations.reason: Catalog entries must state where the definition came from.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The container is a daemon: it runs the fan controller, applies the profile and logs to stdout; it exposes no listening port and no web interface.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: ProxMenux installs it as a non-web application with no frontend endpoint and no published port.
adaptations.reason: A daemon has nothing to browse; the installer shows it as a headless service.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: There is no first-run URL and no credential to recover; all configuration is done through the environment variables at install time.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: When IDRAC_HOST is an IP address, the container drives the iDRAC over IPMI-over-LAN and needs no host device.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: The LXC uses its own address on the selected bridge and reaches the iDRAC over the network like any other client.
adaptations.reason: A dedicated LXC has its own network namespace and does not need the host's IPMI device.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: The profile covers the remote mode only; IDRAC_HOST=local, which needs /dev/ipmi0 passthrough, is not covered and must be configured by hand.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The container relies on two IPMI raw commands Dell removed from recent firmware: they exist on iDRAC 6, 7 and 8, on iDRAC 9 up to firmware 3.30.30.30, and never on iDRAC 10 or on blades and modular servers.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: The container starts, logs the iDRAC firmware version and reports whether the server accepted fan control; it exits cleanly when the commands are refused.
adaptations.reason: The compatibility limit is a property of the iDRAC firmware, not of the container runtime.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: On an iDRAC 9 at 3.34.34.34 or newer, or on any iDRAC 10, the container cannot control the fans and only monitors; the user must not expect the profile to change that.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The container is stateless: every setting comes from environment variables and nothing is written to a volume.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: ProxMenux installs it with no managed volume and no host bind.
adaptations.reason: A daemon with no state has nothing to persist or back up.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: Removing and reinstalling the LXC loses no data; the configuration lives in the environment of the instance.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The project publishes a multi-architecture manifest tagged latest, covering amd64 and arm64.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: The curated profile pins latest and declares both architectures.
adaptations.reason: One catalog entry can name one image reference; the project's own tags are multi-arch.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: The installer resolves the digest for the architecture of the host.

adaptations.upstream_behavior: The container reaches the iDRAC over the network; it publishes no port.
adaptations.native_lxc_behavior: The application uses the address of its own LXC to reach the iDRAC.
adaptations.reason: A native LXC has its own address and does not require Docker port NAT.
adaptations.behavioral_impact: No published port; the installer shows it as a headless service.

compatibility.policy: Single-image definitions are installable when every declared Compose option has a native Proxmox translation. Multi-image and unsupported runtime features remain blocked until their orchestrator or mapping is available.
